newsitem.title: USA: U.S. card issuers down on Advanta woes.
newsitem.headline: U.S. card issuers down on Advanta woes.

text.p: Stocks of the major "monoline" credit card issuers were down on Monday morning in reaction to the woes of Advanta Corp, one of the largest players in the industry, analysts said.
The monoline companies are primarily focused on issuing cards. Advanta surprised Wall Street with news that it expects a loss of $0.44 per share in the first quarter of 1997.

Eric Grubelich, analyst at Keefe, Bruyette & Woods, said companies such as First USA Inc, Capital One Financial Corp and MBNA Corp fell despite different customer profiles and characteristics in their portfolios.
Grubelich said the industry trend to higher delinquencies and higher loss ratios was "not a new piece of news."
Advanta said it expects the loss ratio in its card portfolio to be in the 6.5-7.5 percent range this year. In the first quarter of 1996 the ratio was only 3.2 percent.
"This is what you get when you grow that fast," said George Salem, analyst at Gerard Klauer Mattison.
Grubelich said the Advanta portfolio had rapid growth in the 1995-1996 period, which he said was late in the cycle for the industry.
Advanta was down 9-1/8 to 31-1/2 in late morning. First USA was off 1-3/4 to 48-1/8, Capital One was off 1-3/8 to 37-3/4 and MBNA was off 1-3/4 to 31-5/8.
Banc One Corp, which agreed earlier this year to buy First USA, was off one to 43-5/8.
